named_sites.note: Hours per target are flat (no snow, no terrain), snow_free and open, each for the year and the local winter and summer halves, as every hour ('all') and inside long spells only ('long'). In the south the snow is unmeasured (snow_free is null) and open hours count the terrain only. The *_clear fields are typical clear-sky hours from cells_scored.json (open hours times the monthly clear share).

big_picture_north.note: long_snow_free_hours counts every measured cell over a flat horizon. The two rows 'among cells with a horizon' and the open and clear calendars count only the measured cells that have a terrain horizon. Clear-sky hours are open hours times the monthly mean clear share of the sky; that is not the chance that a low Sun is visible.

terrain_share_left.note: Share = long-window open hours / long-window flat-horizon hours per cell (north: snow-free hours; south: rock-season hours), over the cells of the group that have a horizon and any such hours. blind_sample: the cells candidates.json marks 'sample', drawn before any score was looked at. all_measured / all: every gridded cell of that side. cells_in_group counts the group, horizon.cells those of it with a horizon.

old_against_new.old_note: light_cells_v1.json holds the four regions of the first method only; old is null for the others

stability.note: survivors: baseline top-10 sites that keep a site within 50 km under the change.

haughton_july.note: A NASA-funded rover test used the 24-hour Sun at Haughton crater in July 2001; the hours below are what this method gives for the same place and month.
